Md. Yahya ------ For the Petitioner.

parties:
Mst. Masuda Khatoon & ors  ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
Maniruzzaman  ------ Opposite party.
full_judgment: “If the contention of the learned council that appeal lies under Order 43 Rule 1(d), whether the matter is decided on merits or is dismissed in default, were to prevail, the position will be that in the latter case there will be no evidence before the appellate Court for its scrutiny. On what basis then, can it be decided whether the order of dismissal is corrector not. There is no provision in C. P. C. excepting Order 41 Rule 27, empowering the Appellate Court to record evidence. Order 41 Rule27 empowers them in certain limited case, to record additional evidence, i.e. evidence in addition what is already on record and then too only in that case, where the evidence already on record is found to be either insufficient or not clear enough to enable them to give judgment. In a case where a matter is dismissed for default, there could be no evidence. The question that an Appellate Court will be called upon to decide will be whether or not, the appellant had sufficient cause for his non attendance, and the law does not permit him to lead evidence before me. It is this obstacle which comes in the way of accepting a proposition that an appeal lies whether the decision is on merits or it is on account of non attendance of a party. The proposition, if accepted, will lead to absurd results, and there is always a presumption again absurdity. It cannot, therefore, be said that the respondent had a remedy under Order 43 Rule 1(d).”
